chapters.title: Varaha Avatara — The Rescue of Earth

verses.sanskrit: वाराहं रूपमास्थाय महाविष्णुः प्रजापतिः | रसातलतलं गत्वा उद्धृतां धरणीं ददौ ||
verses.transliteration: vārāhaṃ rūpamāsthāya mahāviṣṇuḥ prajāpatiḥ | rasātalaṃ talaṃ gatvā uddhrītāṃ dharaṇīṃ dadau ||
verses.translation: Taking the form of a boar, the great Vishnu, lord of all creation, descended to the bottom of the netherworld, lifted the Earth, and restored her.
verses.hindi: महाविष्णु ने वाराह रूप धारण किया और रसातल की गहराई में जाकर धरती को उठाकर वापस लाए।
verses.commentary: Three theological movements in one verse: (1) "vārāhaṃ rūpamāsthāya" — taking the form most adapted to the task. Vishnu does not remain in his majestic four-armed form and command the Earth to rise. He becomes a boar — an animal uniquely suited to root through earth and water — because the form of grace must fit the nature of the need. (2) "rasātala talaṃ gatvā" — descending to the very bottom. The divine does not rescue from a safe distance. It goes to the deepest point of the problem. (3) "uddhrītām dharaṇīṃ dadau" — lifted and restored. The Earth is not merely freed from the demon; she is lifted — raised to her proper place — and given back to herself. Rescue is not just removal of harm; it is restoration of dignity.

verses.sanskrit: हिरण्याक्षो महाबाहुः पृथिवीं निह्नुते बली | तमहत्वा महाविष्णुः पृथिवीमुज्जहार ह ||
verses.transliteration: hiraṇyākṣo mahābāhuḥ pṛthivīṃ nihnute balī | tamāhatvā mahāviṣṇuḥ pṛthivīmujjahāra ha ||
verses.translation: The mighty-armed Hiranyaksha, powerful, seizes and submerges the Earth. Slaying him, the great Vishnu lifts the Earth up.
verses.hindi: महाबाहु, बलशाली हिरण्याक्ष ने पृथ्वी को दबा दिया। उसे मारकर महाविष्णु ने पृथ्वी को ऊपर उठाया।
verses.commentary: Hiranyaksha — literally "golden-eyed," the one who sees everything in terms of gold/acquisition — is the mythological form of hoarding, extraction, and the reduction of the sacred to a resource. The Earth (Bhudevi), the principle of patient sustaining, of giving without return, of holding all life, is seized and dragged under by the extractive principle. The cosmic imbalance the Varaha myth describes is directly relevant: when the extractive principle (hiranyākṣa-dharma) overwhelms the sustaining principle (bhudevi-dharma), the entire foundation of life is threatened. Vishnu's response is not negotiation — it is decisive confrontation, followed immediately by restoration.

verses.sanskrit: भूरुवाच: को धर्मः परमो लोके केन मुक्तिः प्रजायते | कथं त्वां पूजयेद् विष्णो यथा मुक्तिः प्रजायते ||
verses.transliteration: bhūruvāca: ko dharmaḥ paramo loke kena muktiḥ prajāyate | kathaṃ tvāṃ pūjayed viṣṇo yathā muktiḥ prajāyate ||
verses.translation: The Earth speaks: What is the highest dharma in the world? By what does liberation arise? How should one worship You, O Vishnu, such that liberation is born?
verses.hindi: भूदेवी बोलीं: इस लोक में परम धर्म क्या है? किससे मुक्ति होती है? हे विष्णो! आपकी पूजा कैसे करें जिससे मुक्ति मिले?
verses.commentary: Three questions from the Earth to Vishnu — and they are the three questions of the entire spiritual tradition: What is the highest dharma? How does liberation arise? What is the correct practice? The Earth asks these questions not in ignorance but in the context of her just-completed ordeal. She has been seized, submerged, and rescued. From this position — having experienced the extremity of both destruction and rescue — she asks about the permanent. The questions gain depth because of who is asking: the Earth, who holds all life, who has experienced the full weight of adharma and the reality of divine rescue, asks for the path that makes rescue permanent.

verses.sanskrit: सर्वभूतहितं धर्मं विष्णुरुवाच महामते | अहिंसा परमो धर्मः सर्वप्राणभृतां वर ||
verses.transliteration: sarvabhūtahitaṃ dharmaṃ viṣṇuruvāca mahāmate | ahiṃsā paramo dharmaḥ sarvapraṇabhṛtāṃ vara ||
verses.translation: Vishnu speaks: O great-minded one, dharma is that which benefits all beings. Non-harm (ahimsa) is the highest dharma for all creatures.
verses.hindi: विष्णु बोले: हे महामते! धर्म वह है जो सभी प्राणियों का हित करे। सभी प्राणियों के लिए अहिंसा परम धर्म है।
verses.commentary: Vishnu's answer to Earth's first question: the highest dharma is "sarvabhūtahita" — the welfare of all beings. Not the welfare of one's own group, tradition, or species, but all beings. The definition is universal and non-sectarian. Then the operational principle: "ahiṃsā paramo dharmaḥ" — non-harm is the highest dharma. This is one of the most cited verses in the Hindu ethical tradition. Its placement here is significant: Vishnu says this to the Earth — who has just experienced the ultimate form of harm. The connection is not accidental: the Earth, who sustains all, needs to hear that the highest dharma for all is to sustain each other by not harming.

chapters.title: Prapatti Yoga — Complete Surrender to Vishnu

verses.sanskrit: स्थाने हृषीकेश तव प्रकीर्त्या जगत्प्रहृष्यत्यनुरज्यते च | रक्षांसि भीतानि दिशो द्रवन्ति सर्वे नमस्यन्ति च सिद्धसङ्घाः ||
verses.transliteration: sthāne hṛṣīkeśa tava prakīrtyā jagatprahṛṣyatyanurajyate ca | rakṣāṃsi bhītāni diśo dravanti sarve namasyanti ca siddhasaṃghāḥ ||
verses.translation: Rightly, O Hrishikesha, the world rejoices and is delighted at Your glory. Demons flee in all directions in fear, and all assemblies of the perfected ones bow to You.
verses.hindi: हे हृषीकेश! आपकी कीर्ति से जगत् प्रसन्न और अनुरक्त होता है — यह उचित ही है। राक्षस भयभीत होकर दिशाओं में भागते हैं, और सिद्धों के समूह आपको नमस्कार करते हैं।
verses.commentary: "Sthāne" — rightly so, fittingly so. The verse opens with an acknowledgment: the world's delight in Vishnu is appropriate, fitting, the natural response to what Vishnu actually is. The world rejoices not because it is required to but because it responds to what is genuinely joyful. The Varaha Purana's prapatti teaching begins here: surrender is not a defeat — it is the appropriate, natural response of all beings to the reality of the divine. The demons' fear and flight, the siddhas' bowing — both are responses to the same reality; one contracts, the other expands. Prapatti is the expanded response.

verses.sanskrit: वराहो भूत्वा विष्णुस्तु भूदेवीं पातालवासिनीम् | उद्धृत्य दंष्ट्रयोर्मूले स्थापयामास पृथ्व्याम् ||
verses.transliteration: varāho bhūtvā viṣṇustu bhūdevīṃ pātālavāsinīm | uddhṛtya daṃṣṭrayormūle sthāpayāmāsa pṛthvyām ||
verses.translation: Vishnu becoming Varaha lifted Bhudevi from her residence in Patala and established her on earth by the roots of his tusks.
verses.hindi: विष्णु वराह बनकर, पाताल में निवास करती हुई भूदेवी को उठाकर, अपने दाँतों के मूल से पृथ्वी पर स्थापित किया।
verses.commentary: The Varaha Purana's central narrative: Vishnu as the boar avatar rescues the Earth (Bhudevi) from the depths of the cosmic ocean (Patala). The image is both literal and symbolic: the divine dives into the depths — the most unconscious, chaotic, submerged aspects of existence — and brings forth the earth, the ground of all manifestation. The tusks (daṃṣṭra) are the instruments of rescue: what appears violent (a boar's tusk) is actually the means of salvation. The Varaha Purana teaches that the divine enters the darkest places to bring forth what has been lost.

verses.sanskrit: आनुकूल्यस्य सङ्कल्पः प्रातिकूल्यस्य वर्जनम् | रक्षिष्यतीति विश्वासो गोप्तृत्वे वरणं तथा ||
verses.transliteration: ānukūlyasya saṃkalpaḥ prātikūlyasya varjanam | rakṣiṣyatīti viśvāso goptṛtve varaṇaṃ tathā ||
verses.translation: The resolve to act in alignment; the abandonment of what opposes; the trust that "He will protect"; and the choice of God as one's protector — these are the limbs of prapatti.
verses.hindi: अनुकूलता का संकल्प, प्रतिकूलता का त्याग, "वह रक्षा करेंगे" यह विश्वास, और गोप्तृत्व के लिए उनका वरण — ये प्रपत्ति के अंग हैं।
verses.commentary: The Varaha Purana provides one of the earliest systematic definitions of prapatti (complete surrender). Four components: (1) Ānu-kūlya-saṃkalpa — resolve to act in alignment with the divine will; (2) Prāti-kūlya-varjana — abandoning what opposes that alignment; (3) Rakṣiṣyatīti viśvāsa — the trust that "He will protect" (not hope or wish but actual trust, grounded in the nature of the protector); (4) Goptṛtve varaṇa — the choice of God as protector (an active choosing, not passive drift). Prapatti is not passive — it has four active components. The passivity is only in the relinquishment of independent ego-agency; the activity is in the alignment, the trust, and the choice.

verses.sanskrit: भूदेवी विष्णुं प्राहु: कथं मुक्तिः प्रजायते | विष्णुरुवाच: भक्तिरेषा मुक्तिः सर्वकर्मभिः ||
verses.transliteration: bhūdevī viṣṇuṃ prāhu: kathaṃ muktiḥ prajāyate | viṣṇuruvāca: bhaktireṣā muktiḥ sarvakarmabhiḥ ||
verses.translation: Bhudevi asked Vishnu: how is liberation attained? Vishnu replied: through this bhakti, liberation is attained from all karma.
verses.hindi: भूदेवी ने विष्णु से पूछा: मुक्ति कैसे प्राप्त होती है? विष्णु ने कहा: इस भक्ति से मुक्ति सभी कर्मों से प्राप्त होती है।
verses.commentary: The Varaha Purana presents a direct dialogue between Bhudevi (the Earth) and Vishnu. The Earth asks the fundamental question: how is liberation attained? Vishnu's answer is simple: through bhakti. The verse specifies that this bhakti liberates from "sarvakarmabhiḥ" — all karma. This is the Varaha Purana's core teaching: bhakti is not merely devotion but the means of complete liberation from the bondage of karma.

verses.sanskrit: धर्मो रक्षति रक्षितः धर्मो हन्ति हतः क्रिया | धर्मो न प्रशश्यते किञ्चित् धर्मेण तप्यते अमृतम् ||
verses.transliteration: dharmo rakṣati rakṣitaḥ dharmaḥ hanti hatāḥ kriyā | dharmaḥ na praśaśyate kiñcid dharmeṇa tapyate amṛtam ||
verses.translation: Dharma protects when protected; dharma destroys when destroyed. Dharma never perishes; through dharma, immortality is attained.
verses.hindi: धर्म रक्षा करता है जब रक्षित होता है; धर्म नष्ट करता है जब नष्ट किया जाता है। धर्म कभी नहीं मरता; धर्म से अमृत प्राप्त होता है।
verses.commentary: The Varaha Purana states the reciprocal nature of dharma: when you protect dharma, dharma protects you; when you destroy dharma, dharma destroys you. This is not a threat but a description of the structure of reality. Dharma is the principle of order; when you align with it, it sustains you; when you violate it, it undermines you. The verse concludes that dharma never perishes — it is eternal — and through dharma, immortality is attained.

verses.sanskrit: सर्वभूतानां हितार्थं विष्णुः सर्वं पालयते | यो विष्णुं भजते भक्त्या स प्राप्नोति परं पदम् ||
verses.transliteration: sarvabhūtānām hitārthaṃ viṣṇuḥ sarvaṃ pālayate | yo viṣṇuṃ bhajate bhaktyā sa prāpnoti paraṃ padam ||
verses.translation: For the welfare of all beings, Vishnu protects all. He who worships Vishnu with devotion attains the supreme state.
verses.hindi: सभी प्राणियों के हित के लिए, विष्णु सब की रक्षा करते हैं। जो विष्णु को भक्ति से भजता है, वह परम पद प्राप्त करता है।
verses.commentary: The Varaha Purana declares that Vishnu protects all beings for their welfare. This is the cosmic principle: Vishnu as the sustainer of all existence. The verse then states that those who worship Vishnu with devotion attain the supreme state — liberation. The connection is clear: by aligning with the one who protects all beings, you participate in that protection and attain the same state.
